find: A doctor who knows that a temperature above 38°C in a newborn requires emergency hospital admission is applying knowledge — rules built on clinical information.
replace: A doctor who knows that a temperature of 38°C or higher in a baby under 3 months needs urgent medical advice is applying knowledge — rules built on clinical information.
note: F1: NHS guidance calls for urgent advice, not automatic hospital admission.

find: Check digits are particularly effective at catching transposition errors (where two digits are accidentally swapped) because swapping changes the calculated total.
replace: A check digit can detect many transposition errors, but not every transposition.
note: F2: ISBN-13/EAN-style check digits do not detect every adjacent transposition.

find: When data travels across a network it is divided into small chunks called packets. Each packet contains the data payload, the destination address, the source address and a sequence number so that packets can be reassembled in the correct order at the other end, even if they travelled by different routes. Packet switching allows networks to be more efficient because different packets can take different routes depending on congestion.
replace: When data travels across a network it is divided into small chunks called packets. Packets carry a data payload and header information such as source and destination addresses. Protocols that need ordered delivery, such as TCP, use sequence numbers so the receiver can reassemble data in the correct order. Packet switching allows networks to be more efficient because different packets can take different routes depending on congestion.
note: F3: Sequence numbers are not present in every IP packet.

find: the cloud provider handles backups, security updates and maintenance.
replace: the provider maintains the underlying infrastructure, while the organisation remains responsible for its data, settings and access controls.
note: F4: Cloud security and maintenance are shared responsibilities.
F4: Cloud use reduces, rather than removes, maintenance responsibilities.

find: Bluetooth</dfn> — connects devices like headphones and keyboards up to around 10 metres;
replace: Bluetooth</dfn> — connects devices like headphones and keyboards over short distances, often around 10 metres;
note: F5: Around 10 metres is common, not Bluetooth's upper limit.

find: Bluetooth works at distances up to around 10 metres and requires a one-time pairing between devices.
replace: Bluetooth often works over distances around 10 metres and usually starts with pairing between devices.
note: F5: Bluetooth range and pairing depend on the implementation.

expect: Short-range wireless connections for headphones and keyboards up to 10 metres.
value: Short-range wireless connections for devices such as headphones and keyboards.
note: F5: Bluetooth does not have a universal 10-metre maximum range.

expect: A short-range wireless standard for connecting devices over distances up to about 10 metres, commonly used for headphones, keyboards and file transfer between phones.
value: A short-range wireless standard commonly used for headphones, keyboards and file transfer between phones.
note: F5: Bluetooth range varies with the implementation and environment.

find: USB-C — a reversible connector with fast speeds and higher power delivery, standard on modern laptops and smartphones;
replace: USB-C — a reversible connector whose data speed and power delivery depend on the USB version and device;
note: F6: USB-C alone does not specify speed or power delivery.

find: Because NFC is so close-range, it is inherently more secure for payment — it is very difficult for an attacker to intercept a signal that only works at a distance of a few centimetres.
replace: Its short range helps prevent accidental connections, but payment security also depends on authentication and encryption.
note: F7: Proximity alone does not make an NFC payment inherently secure.

find: Using a VPN (Virtual Private Network) also encrypts all outgoing traffic, providing protection even on unsecured public networks.
replace: A VPN (Virtual Private Network) can encrypt traffic between your device and the VPN provider, adding protection on unsecured public networks.
note: F8: A VPN protects the tunnel to its provider, not every later connection or risk.

find: satellite — data relayed via an orbiting satellite, enabling remote-area connectivity though with higher latency.
replace: satellite — data relayed via an orbiting satellite, enabling remote-area connectivity; latency depends on the satellite's orbit.
note: F9: Low-Earth-orbit services have lower latency than geostationary services.
